name: Upper/lower split

lead: An upper/lower split divides weight training into upper-body days and lower-body days, usually run four days per week. Each muscle group is trained twice a week, with rest days between sessions.

People use it to build muscle size and strength, which shapes physique, shoulder width and overall build. Training frequency, intensity and volume are described in general references as the variables that drive muscle growth, and this layout is one way to organise them.

paras: A typical week alternates upper and lower sessions with rest days. Lifters on T Nation forums describe it as one of several common splits alongside the bro split and push/pull/legs, and one poster describes running a Wendler 'BBB Opposite' program as essentially an upper-lower split. Results over months depend on progressive overload, food and sleep.

Risks are those of weight training generally: strain and overuse injury if volume or load outstrips recovery. A four-day layout fits many schedules but offers fewer sessions per week than higher-frequency splits.

angle.text: The split is a way to schedule training so that each muscle group gets work twice a week. People use it to build shoulders, back, arms and legs for a more muscular physique.

lead: An upper/lower split is a weight-training layout that alternates sessions for the upper body and the lower body, commonly four days per week. It is discussed on T Nation alongside the bro split and the push/pull/legs split [1]. Each muscle group is trained about twice weekly under this layout.

People use it to gain muscle, strength and shape. A general reference on muscle hypertrophy names training frequency, intensity and total volume as variables that affect muscle growth, and says gradually increasing them yields hypertrophy [2]. The same reference says long-term gains seem to depend more on total training volume and progressive overload than on rep tempo [2].
Lifters on forums describe adapting programs into this shape; one poster says that doing a Wendler 'BBB Opposite' program is essentially an upper-lower split, running it with modifications [3].
infobox: About twice weekly per muscle group

paras: The upper/lower split assigns pressing, pulling and arm work to upper days and squats, hinges and leg work to lower days. A typical week runs two of each, separated by rest days. T Nation forum posts name it as a common choice beside the bro split and push/pull/legs [1].

The general reference on muscle hypertrophy lists frequency, intensity and total volume as training variables that directly affect growth [2]. Splits such as this one are a way to spread that volume across the week, with each muscle trained twice rather than once, as in a bro split.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and lifting communities
paras: Lifters describe the layout in training logs and program discussions; some say a program is 'essentially' an upper-lower split when it alternates upper and lower focus [3].
No studies found on the upper/lower split as a named program. General research on training frequency and volume exists but is not summarised here.
